clue.text: Dismiss objection — you blew it!

parts.note: to dismiss someone from a job is to sack them
a 'but' is an objection, as in 'no ifs or buts'

explanation.surface: Someone is fired, protests, and is told the blunder was entirely their own fault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'you blew it!' reads as a reproach, but it addresses the instrument: a player blows into it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sackbut is an early form of trombone, a brass instrument played by blowing.

clue.text: See 3
French horn gets on with a trumpet

parts.note: cor is the French word for horn
taken as written

explanation.surface: A French horn joins in alongside a trumpet in the orchestra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French horn' looks like the instrument, but it means the French word for horn. 'gets' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The corona is the botanical name for the trumpet-shaped centre of a daffodil.

clue.text: Drink in bed

definitions.meaning: a classic cocktail of brandy, rum, triple sec and lemon carries this name
tucked up under the bedclothes, lying in bed

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a known cocktail and also literally describes lying between the bedclothes.

clue.text: One might be running up into cupola to theologise

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top
into signals letters found inside the following words

explanation.surface: Someone climbs into a church dome to ponder God.
explanation.walkthrough: LATOT sits inside 'cupoLA TO Theologise'; 'up' turns it round. 'running up' looks like one phrase, but 'running' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A running total is one kept up to date as items are added.

clue.text: Plant's success rate of insecticide?

definitions.meaning: a plant of the borage family with bristly leaves
an insecticide's success is measured by how many insects it kills, read as two words: insect loss

explanation.definitionFit: Bugloss is the name of several rough-leaved plants of the borage family.

clue.text: Baton said to be used in torture

indicators.note: the letters are to be worked over and turned into something new

explanation.surface: A truncheon is said to have been employed by torturers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be used' rearranges BATON and SAID; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The bastinado is a torture of beating the soles of the feet with a stick.

clue.text: Swot up about a Pacific island

indicators.note: about means going around the letter that follows
in a down clue, up means the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: to mug up is British slang for studying hard, so a swot is a mug

explanation.surface: A student is told to revise all about an island in the Pacific.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns MUG into GUM, and 'about' puts it around A. 'Swot up' looks like the phrase meaning to study, but 'up' is the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Guam is a US territory in the Mariana Islands of the western Pacific.

clue.text: These eccentric first, third and fifth deliveries?

definitions.meaning: eccentric people, as a plural noun
in cricket the balls of an over numbered one, three and five are the odd-numbered ones

explanation.definitionFit: Oddballs are eccentric people, and read as two words it describes the odd-numbered balls of a cricket over.

clue.text: Against reforms, old South American city

indicators.note: reforms means the letters of the preceding word are reshaped

explanation.surface: Opponents of political change remember an old city in South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Against' looks like part of the surface's politics, but its letters are the fodder that 'reforms' reshapes.
explanation.definitionFit: Santiago is the capital of Chile, a city in South America.

clue.text: Bird, one of Sinatra's few, decapitated

indicators.note: decapitated means the head, the first letter, is removed

parts.note: in My Way, Sinatra sings 'regrets, I've had a few'

explanation.surface: A bird appears as one of Frank Sinatra's few, with its head cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: The song My Way runs 'Regrets, I've had a few'; take the head off REGRET.
explanation.definitionFit: An egret is a white heron, a wading bird.

clue.text: See 14
Squiggly red line not cut

indicators.note: squiggly means wavy and twisted, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A wavy red line drawn on a page has not been cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Squiggly' rearranges RED LINE NOT. 'cut' looks like it continues 'not', but it is the definition: a cut of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenderloin is a prized cut of beef or pork from along the loin.

clue.text: Island offering a taste of cannibalism

indicators.note: a taste is a small portion taken from within the word that follows

explanation.surface: An island serves up a sample of cannibalism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offering' is a link. The letters sit in 'canniBALIsm'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bali is an Indonesian island east of Java.

clue.text: Community decision

definitions.meaning: a place where people have settled and live together, such as a village
an agreement that resolves a dispute, as in an out-of-court deal

explanation.definitionFit: A settlement is both a small community of settlers and an agreed resolution of a dispute.

clue.text: Lack any evidence, so be forced to lie?

definitions.meaning: to have no proof to support one's case
literally lacking a limb ..., one would have to lie down

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to have no support for an argument; read literally, someone without a leg must lie down.

clue.text: Irritable, accepting single day for evidence

indicators.note: accepting means taking the following letters inside

parts.note: testy means irritable and short-tempered
I is the Roman numeral one, a single
Mon is the usual abbreviation for Monday

explanation.surface: A grumpy witness agrees to give one day's evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'single' is the Roman numeral one; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Testimony is evidence given by a witness, especially under oath.

clue.text: Article is enabled, so it grows

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
can means is able to
thus and so both mean therefore

explanation.surface: A newspaper article is published and so its readership grows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' suggests writing, but it is the grammatical article A.
explanation.definitionFit: Acanthus is a plant, so it is something that grows; its leaves inspired Corinthian capitals.

clue.text: Come across behind horse

parts.note: bum is British slang for the backside, one's behind
a pinto is a piebald horse

explanation.surface: Someone happens upon a rider at the back of a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: To bump into someone is to come across them by chance.

clue.text: Unable to reach toilet, has taken wee

parts.note: caught means taken, as in captured
wee is Scottish for small, so short

explanation.surface: Someone who could not reach the lavatory has had an accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wee' looks like urination in this toilet scene, but it means small. 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being caught short is the idiom for urgently needing a toilet with none to hand.

clue.text: Why Saatchi left Saatchi alone?

definitions.meaning: Maurice Saatchi split from the agency Saatchi & Saatchi; read as two words, the cause was a drift apart
cut loose and on one's own, without moorings

explanation.definitionFit: Adrift means drifting alone and unanchored, and split as two words names a gradual parting of ways.

clue.text: Speaker sees climbing marsupial pouching animal

indicators.note: pouching means holding inside, as a marsupial carries young in a pouch
in a down clue, climbing means the word is read upwards

parts.note: roo is short for kangaroo, a marsupial
a rat is an animal

explanation.surface: A speaker observes a kangaroo climbing with another animal in its pouch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns the marsupial into OOR before 'pouching' wraps it round the animal. 'sees' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An orator is a public speaker, especially an eloquent one.

clue.text: Denial honest, then back to front

indicators.note: back to front means the last letter is moved to the front

parts.note: open means honest and frank

explanation.surface: A denial is honest, and then turned around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back to front' moves the N of OPEN to the start; 'then' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Nope is a casual way of saying no, a denial.

clue.text: Underground worker filled with horror — our thoughts are with him?

indicators.note: filled with means the following word goes inside

parts.note: a miner works underground
dread is horror or great fear

explanation.surface: A trapped miner is gripped by fear, and our thoughts are with him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'our thoughts are with him' sounds like sympathy for the miner, but it means he has access to what we think.
explanation.definitionFit: A mind-reader is a telepath who supposedly knows what others are thinking.

clue.text: One removes water as doctor drinks old port

indicators.note: drinks means takes in, so the second piece goes inside

parts.note: Rye in Sussex is an old Cinque Port, now silted up and inland

explanation.surface: A doctor drinks vintage port, while something takes away water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old port' looks like a drink, but it is Rye, one of England's historic Cinque Ports. 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A dryer is a machine that removes water from clothes or hair.

clue.text: Growth starts to tell, seeing your carnations coming up

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the letters read upwards
starts to means the first letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A gardener describes signs of growth as the carnations come up.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letters give TSYC, which 'coming up' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: A cyst is an abnormal growth, a sac in body tissue.

clue.text: Fine, macho swimmer

parts.note: hunky means muscular and manly
a dory is a fish, so a swimmer

explanation.surface: A fine, muscular man is a good swimmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimmer' suggests a person, but it is a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunky-dory is informal for fine or satisfactory.

clue.text: Live figure almost snatching another back

indicators.note: back means the whole result is read in reverse
snatching means seizing and holding the following piece inside
almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: ten is a figure, a number
six is another figure

explanation.surface: A living figure nearly grabs another back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' leaves TE; 'snatching' gives TSIXE; 'back' reverses the whole. 'another' means another figure.
explanation.definitionFit: To exist is to live or be alive.

clue.text: Anon ano?

definitions.meaning: the clue word is the preceding word shortened, so it is that word written briefly

explanation.definitionFit: Anon means soon, in a short while; and the second word is the first done in a cut-down way.

clue.text: What may swivel, may swivel

indicators.note: the repeated words say the answer can be turned round and still read the same

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A thing that may swivel, may swivel.
explanation.walkthrough: The repetition hints that the answer reads the same when turned backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotator is something that turns or rotates, such as a muscle or device.
